instruction: run.sh runs three 1-second sleep jobs sequentially (takes ~3s). Rewrite it to run them in parallel (all three as background jobs + wait), so it finishes in ~1s and still writes done to done.txt when all complete.
setup:
cat > run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
sleep 1 && echo a >> jobs.txt
sleep 1 && echo b >> jobs.txt
sleep 1 && echo c >> jobs.txt
echo done > done.txt
EOF
chmod +x run.sh

grader.script: rm -f jobs.txt done.txt && START=$(date +%s) && bash run.sh && END=$(date +%s) && [ $((END-START)) -le 2 ] && [ "$(sort jobs.txt | tr -d '\n')" = abc ] && grep -qx done done.txt

oracle.script:
cat > run.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
sleep 1 && echo a >> jobs.txt &
sleep 1 && echo b >> jobs.txt &
sleep 1 && echo c >> jobs.txt &
wait
echo done > done.txt
EOF
rm -f jobs.txt done.txt && bash run.sh
